behavioral_observations.observation: Amiens generates 2.4 big chances/game at home (long_run_home) vs 1.0 away (long_run_away) — a large home quality advantage. Recent last 5 shows only 1.4 big chances/game (all venues), but last 5 includes away matches.
Lavallois concedes 2.21 big chances/game long-run (2.43 away) — above Amiens' home generation rate of 2.4, suggesting Lavallois is not a particularly tight defense in terms of big chance suppression.

final_candidate.falsifiable_question: Does Amiens generate more big_chances and shots_on_target at home against opponents whose defensive profile resembles Lavallois' away defensive output, compared to Amiens' overall home baseline?
final_candidate.falsifier: If Amiens' big_chances_for and shots_on_target_for at home against similar-profile opponents are not higher than their overall home baseline, the profile-conditional attack quality mechanism is unsupported.
final_candidate.football_mechanism: Amiens' home big chance generation (2.4/game) meets Lavallois' away big chance concession (2.43/game) — both figures are aligned, suggesting the matchup may produce a normal or above-normal big chance environment for Amiens. The question is whether Amiens' home big chance generation is specifically elevated against opponents who concede big chances at a HIGH rate, which would confirm a profile-conditional quality effect.

self_critique.notes: Combines venue conditioning with opponent defensive profile (big chances conceded axis) to test whether Amiens' home attack quality is specifically elevated against permissive defenses. The mechanism requires both conditions simultaneously. The explicit opponent_profile condition on the defensive axis is the structural increment over the generic structures.

final_candidate.similar_opponent_rationale: Lavallois away concedes big chances at a rate above the median. The similar-opponent cohort identifies prior Amiens home opponents with a comparable defensive profile (big chances conceded, shots on target conceded), allowing measurement of whether Amiens' home big chance and shots on target generation is elevated against such opponents.
final_candidate.subject: TEAM_A

incremental_structure: dual target_metric: big_chances AND shots_on_target tested jointly (not separately)
opponent_profile condition on TEAM_B's defensive axis (big chances conceded / shots on target conceded) as the cohort-defining similarity dimension
mechanism requires BOTH venue conditioning AND opponent defensive profile to hold simultaneously — not either alone
similar_opponent_rationale anchored to TEAM_B's specific away defensive output, not generic opponent strength
response.reason: All three generic structures test a single metric (big_chances or shots_on_target) for the home team against a similar-opponent cohort at home. C11 is structurally distinct in two ways: (1) it tests two metrics jointly (big_chances AND shots_on_target) as a combined attack-quality signal rather than either metric in isolation, and (2) it adds an explicit opponent_profile axis — the cohort is defined by TEAM_B's away defensive permissiveness on those same metrics, not just generic opponent similarity. This creates a two-dimensional conditioning structure (venue × opponent defensive profile) that none of the three generic structures carry. The mechanism requires both conditions to hold simultaneously, which is a different statistical question from any single-metric, single-condition generic.
